verdict: Yes, once a Claude model classifies. Holistic classification with Claude Haiku 5.5 got 0.80 of DocSplit sections exactly right, against 0.52 for the default (Amazon Nova 2 Lite, page by page), at about the same cost ($470 against $493 per 1,000 packets). With Claude Sonnet 5.5 it got 0.90, for about $200 more per 1,000 packets. Holistic wins on finding where each document starts (boundary accuracy 0.92 with Claude Sonnet 5.5, against 0.75 page by page); once a document is found, every setup names it correctly (label accuracy 0.86 to 0.99). With Amazon Nova 2 Lite holistic barely helps, and splitting page by page first does a little better (0.65).
